purpose: Market test of Double Heston vs Single Heston vs Black-Scholes on Bitcoin options, in periods where a two-timescale variance structure should matter, with every model fully calibrated per date. Rules fixed before any option surface is fetched or any model fitted.
convention: Deribit quotes option prices in BTC as the Black-76 USD price divided by that expiry's futures price, with no discounting. The BTC price is therefore the forward-normalised option price. Calls are used directly; puts are converted with c = p + 1 - K/F. USD value = normalised price x F.
forward: Per trade, solve for F from (trade price, trade iv, K, tau) under the convention. Per expiry, take the median of F/index over that expiry's trades in the window. Each quote's forward is that ratio times the index at its own trade time.
quote: Last trade per instrument in the window. Primary target: trade price. Secondary robustness target: the exchange mark price at that trade.

date_rule.split: chronological: the earliest 30% of shock episodes (rounded down) and of calm dates are validation; the rest are test
date_rule.unavailable_dates: disclosed; never replaced by other dates

designs.B_heldout_expiries: PRIMARY. Sort a date's expiries by maturity; hold out every odd-ranked expiry except the longest. Calibrate on the remaining expiries (all strikes); score all quotes of held-out expiries. Tests term-structure interpolation, where a second timescale should matter.
designs.A_heldout_strikes: SECONDARY. Within each expiry, sort by strike; hold out odd-ranked strikes. Calibrate on the rest; score held-out strikes.

models.BS_TERM: One Black-76 volatility per calibration expiry. Held-out expiries use linear interpolation in total variance between neighbouring calibration expiries, with constant-volatility extrapolation at the ends. Strongest non-leaking Black-Scholes; no held-out quote informs its own price.
models.SH: Heston, all five parameters (kappa, theta, sigma, rho, v0) calibrated per date and design.
models.DH: Double Heston, separable four-shock literature_exact convention (independent rho_i, |rho_i|<1, no joint disk), slow-first ordering kappa_slow < kappa_fast, all ten parameters calibrated per date and design.

variants.feller_strict: sigma_i = eta_i * sqrt(2 kappa_i theta_i), eta_i in [0.01, 0.999]
variants.feller_free: log sigma_i free in [log 0.01, log 10]; characteristic function remains valid without Feller

variant_selection: For SH and DH separately, choose feller_strict or feller_free by the lower median held-out IV RMSE over all validation dates and both designs. Frozen in variant_selection.json before any test-date fit.
objective: Mean squared vega-weighted price residual, (model - market)/vega, with vega the market Black-76 vega in forward units, floored at 1e-4. This is approximately an implied-vol residual. Identical for every model.

optimizer.convergence: Report all starts; count successful starts within max(1e-12, 1% of the best objective). Never claim a proven global optimum.

numerics.fallback: In evaluation, any 96/128 disagreement above tolerance or bound breach uses the independent adaptive quadrature; every fallback is logged.

primary_endpoint: Shock-regime TEST dates, design B. For each test episode, average the per-date paired differences in held-out IV RMSE: SH minus DH and BS_TERM minus DH. DH beats a competitor only if the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test over test episodes gives p < 0.05 AND the episode-cluster bootstrap 95% lower bound of the mean difference is > 0 (5,000 replicates, seed 20260920).
secondary: design A on shock test dates
both designs on calm test dates (control; a smaller DH advantage is expected)
integrity: Dates come from DVOL alone before any option data is fetched; the calm control set is reported alongside.
No filter, split, metric, bound, optimizer setting or endpoint changes after test fits are seen.
Validation dates are used only for the Feller variant choice.
Failed dates, fits and fallbacks are retained and disclosed.
Trade prices are not synchronized bid/ask; no spread-based claims.
